text: The Patriots' offensive nightmare deepened this week as the team placed guard Greg Van Roten on injured reserve with a thigh injury—another blow to an already beleaguered offensive line protecting Drake Maye—while releasing linebacker Riley Wilson from the practice squad in corresponding moves that underscore the roster instability surrounding the quarterback. The offensive troubles are impossible to ignore: New England ranks dead last in the NFL with just 9.7 points per game, a number that looks even more damning after Sunday's 35-6 demolition at the hands of the Jaguars, in which Lawrence threw three touchdown passes and the Patriots' defense was helpless to stop Jacksonville's assault. Maye himself acknowledged the grim reality, taking ownership of his two interceptions and fumble by calling the offense's performance "unacceptable" and promising to look inward for solutions, though film breakdowns and strategic analyses are raising broader questions about whether the organization is deploying him correctly. This Sunday's road test against Buffalo at 1 PM ET offers no respite—the Bills are hardly a forgiving opponent for a team searching for answers on both sides of the ball.
